This discovery is crucial for sales, innovation, and marketing managers, suggesting that relying solely on selling capabilities might be insufficient. We recommend the integration of additional strategies, such as assertive listening, to enhance knowledge transfer. Such strategies can prevent the pitfalls of overreliance on selling capabilities alone and foster a more effective adoption of industrial innovations among business customers. Our findings offer valuable insights for professionals aiming to navigate the complexities of selling industrial innovations in the digital age, providing a nuanced understanding of how to tailor their approach to improve customer receptivity and adoption rates. 1. This research is pioneering in empirically establishing that the adoption of knowledge by customers acts as a mediating factor between salespeople's selling capabilities and the purchase of innovations. Intriguingly, our findings reveal the existence of an optimal level of selling capability necessary for effective knowledge transfer, which varies depending on specific contingencies. results.content:
Far too often, sales professionals unconsciously focus their discovery/qualification questions on what they care about most; generally BANT, functional requirements and solution fit. Prospects on the other hand care most about the business drivers that are FORCING them to replace their existing business system and the risk of selecting the wrong solution. [...] 2. Project Lead (PL) Engagement Project leads (PL) are typically responsible for managing both the selection process and vendor relationships, making them the first point of contact for almost all opportunities. The primary objective of the qualify stage (see Emotional Discovery Application Points in the Cloud SureStep Sales Process diagram above) is to create a solution and sales professional “bias” in your favor. While there are a number of activities within the within the Qualify phase, the discovery the discovery process is the most important as it dictates both the prospect’s perception and the sales professionals’ understanding of the project. If sales professionals do not understand the emotional and business drivers behind the projects they pursue they will not be able to [...] 1 Remaining Relevant!
Buyer behavior has reshaped prospect qualification and project discovery, leaving little time for sales professionals to influence and bias the selection process. The two most important points of influence in the buying journey now occur at the beginning and at the end of the prospect engagement process—during Qualify and Close. In order to balance out their traditional business process discovery, solution definition and demonstration preparation skills (middle of the sales cycle) sales professionals now need to develop equally strong capabilities on either end.
